decisions.title: Treat DueSoon as a learning build
decisions.choice: Proceed on a narrow v1 for pipeline testing, not as a validated business
decisions.why: No demand evidence; owner asked for a pipeline dry run

decisions.title: Runtime and stack
decisions.choice: Node 22, Express 5, node:sqlite, zod, bcryptjs, express-session; tests with node:test
decisions.why: Few dependencies, runnable in the sandbox; assumed for dogfood (owner not consulted)

decisions.title: Tenancy model
decisions.choice: Individual accounts: every row owned by user_id; cross-user access returns 404
decisions.why: Smallest model for a student tool; assumed for dogfood

decisions.title: Sessions and database limits accepted for v1
decisions.choice: Memory sessions and SQLite on one instance
decisions.why: Zero ops; documented as the first thing to change before scaling

decisions.title: No password recovery or email verification in v1
decisions.choice: Accept: forgotten password loses the account; signup reveals registered emails
decisions.why: Email flows are out of scope; flagged by design review; mitigated by signup rate limit

decisions.title: node:sqlite fallback and Node pin
decisions.choice: Pin Node 22 via engines and .nvmrc; better-sqlite3 is the fallback
decisions.why: node:sqlite is experimental; flagged by design review

decisions.title: Keep can() and structured logging despite review advice to drop them
decisions.choice: Keep both; every query is also scoped by user_id
decisions.why: HyperSkill rules require a central authorisation function and structured logs; cheap at this size

decisions.title: Design direction voice: taste-skill
decisions.choice: taste-skill sets direction; ui-ux-pro-max disabled for this project; impeccable only critiques; emil only motion
decisions.why: HyperSkill rule: one design-direction voice per project; both are installed

decisions.title: Dev dependencies for browser tests
decisions.choice: Add playwright-core and axe-core as devDependencies; e2e runs against the system Chromium (no browser download)
decisions.why: The playbook requires e2e tests for critical flows and an automated accessibility check; assumed for dogfood (owner not consulted)
